hypothesis: Spending more work in the mixer cascade may reduce payload size. Raise the skip confidence threshold from 8 to 9, or disable adaptive skips with threshold 31 (the predictor logit is clamped to +/-30).
unchanged: Same upstream-projected canonical inputs, model weights, dictionary, default link context, online learning rules, fixture phases and compiler settings. One constant in src/adaptive_depth.h changes per candidate.

runner_control.changes: Shared benchmark now records Linux CPU identity; same round-trip procedure.

acceptance: Prepared stream and original XML restored exactly
Only declared threshold source difference against baseline
Retain every result on both reused fixtures, including losses
promotion: Only candidates improving both reused fixtures proceed to the predeclared 80,000,000-byte-offset confirmation range; Linux ranking and full package accounting are still required.
timing: Concurrent native screen times are exploratory. Any candidate needs serial paired Linux timing and full-run eligibility before claiming a useful size/time tradeoff.
limitations: The disabled control still computes and trains the small gate; it measures routing through the full mixer, not removal of gate overhead.
The existing character-rate shortcut remains active; no adaptive skip does not mean every bit executes all models.
Changing which bits train the mixer and BITLSTM changes future model state; more computation need not improve size.
Upstream reports only about 18 KB estimated full-stream cost for adaptive skipping; this alone is not a plausible prize-winning margin.
Small reused fixture results can differ from a full stream; the third range at offset 80,000,000 remains untouched unless both fixtures improve.
source_rationale: Pinned engines/cmix-neif/README.md section 3.4 reports ~2.7 KB cost on an 80 MB window and ~5.1% fewer instructions. These are upstream claims, not locally reproduced performance results.
platform_scope: Native Linux x86-64, all models serial on one CI host; not a full prize run
